articles.title: Star-B-Q 06
articles.summary: The article reports on "Star-B-Q 06," an outdoor social event for an astronomy club, likely the SJAA, in October 2006. It features various members, including SJAA President Mike Koop, participating in activities like a trivia contest and discussions about the Fremont Peak Observatory, alongside a quick-forming chow line.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article discusses the controversial IAU decision to demote Pluto to a "dwarf planet," highlighting the confusing new definition and the widespread disagreement among scientists regarding its flaws and the voting process. It also provides an update on Pluto's current astronomical location in Ophiuchus and offers observing notes for various planets, clarifying previous errors about Uranus's position.

articles.title: A Club Observatory, tale from San Diego
articles.summary: The article describes the San Diego Astronomical Association's (SDAA) Tierra Del Sol observatory site, a 10-acre facility established 30 years ago. Located 70 miles east of San Diego, it offers a developed dark-sky area for public star parties, a club observatory, and various private observing pads and observatories for members. Its success is attributed to strategic site selection, robust infrastructure (electricity, water, restrooms), diverse offerings for members, and continuous volunteer efforts over decades.

articles.title: Alex Filippenko on Dark Energy on October 4, 2006
articles.summary: Astronomer Alex Filippenko of UC Berkeley is scheduled to give a non-technical, illustrated talk titled "Dark Energy and the Runaway Universe" on October 4, 2006, at Foothill College. The lecture will present compelling evidence for the universe's accelerating expansion, driven by mysterious 'dark energy,' a finding in which Dr. Filippenko's group played a leading role. This free public event is part of the Silicon Valley Astronomy Lectures, offering a progress report on the universe's unexpected behavior.

articles.title: Planetary Insights
articles.summary: One article argues for a "Pluto Exception" to the IAU's new planet definition, citing historical precedents and Pluto's unique scientific and cultural significance to retain its planetary status. The second article explores the discovery and formation of "deadly planets" orbiting pulsars, detailing their extreme radiation environments and how observations from the Spitzer Space Telescope reveal they likely form from post-supernova "fallback" disks.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides a detailed status update for its loaner telescope program, listing a wide array of telescopes available for immediate loan to members, along with contact information for the program coordinator, Mike Koop. The document also categorizes scopes currently on loan and those with extended loan periods, informing members about availability and waitlist procedures. The waiting list for new reservations is currently empty.
